text:
maya-cs: Hey — client (AcmeRetail) opened a ticket saying our /v1/rerank responses contain negative values and values > 1. They assumed these were probabilities and it broke their downstream logic. Also they reported occasional 401s for identical requests. Can eng help clarify semantics and give a small repro they can run?

sam-ml: short answer: rerank returns unnormalized scores (logits) by design. Negative values are expected. If you need probs, apply softmax client-side (or we can add a normalized-output option to docs/todo). 401s smell like auth token refresh issues, not related to scoring.

maya-cs: here's the payload they pasted (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "rerank-v1",
    "query": "best running shoes",
    "candidates": [
      {"id": "d1", "text": "Trail-running shoes with grip"},
      {"id": "d2", "text": "Lightweight road shoes"}
    ]
  }'
```
Example response excerpt they shared: `[{"id":"d1","score":-1.23},{"id":"d2","score":0.87}]` — they expected d1+d2 ~= 1.0 or both between 0 and 1.

oliver-engineering: confirming sam's note. Those scores are logits / model affinity scores, not probabilities. They can be negative, zero, positive; their magnitude is relative. Two quick points to check: 1) make sure the client isn't summing scores across different queries or batches; 2) padding/order can shift distributions if they tried to normalize across varying candidate sets.

jess-support: on the 401s — did they get a consistent error body? sometimes we see short-lived 401 spikes when service-account keys rotate or when client's clock is out-of-sync with our auth issuer (signed tokens time-limited). Ask them for the exact error payload and whether they are caching tokens.

oliver-engineering: repro snippet to convert to probabilities (python):
```python
import math
logits = [-1.23, 0.87]
max_l = max(logits)
exps = [math.exp(l - max_l) for l in logits]
probs = [e / sum(exps) for e in exps]
print(probs)  # now sums to 1.0
```
Notes for the client: 1) Apply softmax per candidate set (per query) if you want a 0-1 distribution. 2) If you need a bounded 0-1 per-document score independent of others, consider mapping with sigmoid on each logit (but that changes semantics). 3) If their downstream expects probabilities across a fixed taxonomy, do softmax over that candidate group.

maya-cs: great, I'll pass that along. Client also asked whether this behavior changed recently — anything we deployed that could flip score scale?

sam-ml: nothing recent that flips raw scoring semantics. We did a minor kernel update last week but that shouldn't change logits ordering/scale. I'll open an internal ticket to double-check model config and compare historical runs.

maya-cs: also asked for a quick repro kit they can run locally to prove this — any objection to me sending the python snippet + curl above?

oliver-engineering: go ahead. recommend adding a tiny test harness that posts the same candidate set multiple times (to check determinism) and also a loop that refreshes the bearer token to reproduce 401s if they see them.

sam-ml: I'll create a short doc blurb clarifying "rerank returns unnormalized model scores (logits) — negative values expected" and add the softmax snippet. Filing GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/4678 (internal). :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: token-rotation-job ran at 2024-10-02T03:10:12Z, no errors. If client still sees 401s after token refresh/retry, collect full x-request-id and logs and escalate to auth-team.

maya-cs: perfect — will send to client and ask for their x-request-id + raw error bodies for any 401s. thanks everyone :pray:
